newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU to seek speedy decision on gene maize.
newsitem.headline: EU to seek speedy decision on gene maize.

text.p: European Union Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard will push on Wednesday for scientists to report before the end of October on the safety of Ciba-Geigy's genetically modified maize, a spokesman said.
The move is an attempt to speed up an EU decision on whether a gene-modified maize produced by THE Swiss chemical company is safe for cultivation by EU farmers.
"She's pushing for these assessments to be made as speedily as possible," a Commission spokesman told reporters on the margins of Tuesday's EU environment ministers meeting.
He could not say when the EU executive would reach a final decision on whether or not to approve the corn strain.
Bjerregaard told environment ministers that she would urge fellow Commissioners to back her call for urgency during Wednesday's regular weekly meeting in Brussels, he said.

Delays to the EU's approval process have raised the prospect of trade friction with the U.S., whose farmers plan to export the same maize strain to the 15-country bloc once they have completed this year's harvest.
The Ciba corn has been modified to be resistant to certain pesticides and to the European corn borer pest, which destroys significant parts of the European harvest.

Some EU countries, such as Austria and Sweden, are worried that not enough is known about the possible effects of releasing such products to the environment and fear pesticide-resistant plants may return as "super weeds" when other crops are grown.
